questions.stem: Which of the following is a typical physical property of metals?

options.text: They are good conductors of heat and electricity
They are brittle and shatter when hammered
They are poor conductors of electricity

questions.explanation: Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity due to the delocalised electrons in metallic bonding. They are also generally malleable, ductile, and have high melting points.

questions.stem: Where is the dividing line between metals and non-metals in the periodic table?

options.text: A stepped line going from top-left to bottom-right, with metals on the left
A horizontal line across the middle
A stepped line going from top-right to bottom-left

questions.explanation: A stepped diagonal line runs from the top-left area to the bottom-right of the periodic table. Metals are found to the left and below this line, non-metals to the right and above.

options.text: Lose electrons to form positive ions
Share electrons to form covalent bonds
Do not form ions at all
Gain electrons to form negative ions

questions.explanation: Metals have few outer shell electrons which they lose during reactions to form positive ions (cations). This is in contrast to non-metals, which tend to gain electrons.

questions.stem: What type of oxide do non-metals typically form?
questions.explanation: Non-metal oxides are typically acidic. For example, sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) dissolve in water to form acidic solutions.

questions.stem: Which non-metal is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Graphite is an exception to the rule that non-metals are poor conductors. It conducts electricity because it has delocalised electrons that are free to move between its layers.

options.text: Elements that do not exist naturally
Elements found along the metal/non-metal boundary that have properties of both

questions.explanation: Metalloids (semi-metals) are elements found along the boundary between metals and non-metals. They have some properties of each, for example silicon is a semiconductor.

questions.stem: Metal oxides are typically basic. What happens when a basic oxide reacts with an acid?

options.text: It produces a salt and water (neutralisation)

questions.explanation: Basic metal oxides react with acids in a neutralisation reaction to form a salt and water. For example, CuO + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂O.
